name: GPT-5
one_liner: OpenAI's flagship reasoning + agent model.
summary: OpenAI's frontier model as of 2026. Strong on long-horizon reasoning and tool use; the default choice when you want the most capable closed-weight model and don't mind hosted-only.

name: Claude Sonnet 4.6
one_liner: Anthropic's flagship model — best-in-class for code-heavy agent loops.
summary: Claude Sonnet 4.6 is Anthropic's frontier model in 2026. Default choice for code-generation agents (Claude Code is built on it), tool use is reliable, prompt-injection resistance is strong.

name: Gemini 2.5 Pro
one_liner: Google's flagship long-context multimodal model.
summary: Gemini 2.5 Pro's edge is the long context window (1M+ tokens) and native multimodal handling. Strong choice when document-heavy or video-input workloads dominate.

name: Qwen3-4B-Instruct
one_liner: Open-weight 4B Qwen base — the workhorse for fine-tuning experiments.
summary: Open-weight 4B-parameter instruction-tuned model from Alibaba's Qwen team. The default base model for RL fine-tuning on Tinker because it's small enough to iterate fast and capable enough to follow tool-call schemas.

name: OpenAI Python SDK
one_liner: Official Python client for the OpenAI API.
summary: The official Python client. Streaming, tool calls, structured outputs, batch API. Battle-tested. Use this directly for simple cases; reach for Vercel AI SDK or Agents SDK once you need orchestration.

name: Anthropic Python SDK
one_liner: Official Python client for the Claude API.
summary: Official Anthropic SDK. Streaming, tool calls, computer use, vision. Counterpart to Anthropic's TypeScript SDK; both are production-stable.

name: Vercel AI SDK
one_liner: TypeScript SDK for streaming AI UIs and tool-using agents.
summary: The cleanest TS abstraction for building streaming chat UIs and tool-using agents on top of any model provider. Pairs naturally with Next.js + Vercel hosting; produces production-grade streaming UIs out of the box.

name: OpenAI Agents SDK
one_liner: Official OpenAI SDK for building autonomous tool-using agents.
summary: OpenAI's first-party Python (and TS) SDK for agent loops: tool registration, handoffs between agents, structured outputs, automatic retry. The official path if you're committed to OpenAI models.

name: Claude Agent SDK
one_liner: Anthropic SDK for building autonomous agents on Claude.
summary: Anthropic's SDK for autonomous agents — what powers Claude Code. Strong tool-use loop, native MCP server registration, file system + bash + web search out of the box. Best-in-class for code-heavy or long-running agents.

name: LangGraph
one_liner: Stateful, graph-based agent orchestration from LangChain.
summary: Models agent loops as graphs of nodes (tools, conditions, supervisors). More verbose than CrewAI but gives you structured retry, branching, and human-in-the-loop primitives. Good for complex multi-step flows.

name: CrewAI
one_liner: Multi-agent collaboration framework — give roles, get crews.
summary: Compose specialised agents into a 'crew' with explicit roles, goals, and tasks. The abstraction is friendly for teams new to agent building; less control than LangGraph but faster time-to-prototype.

name: Mastra
one_liner: TypeScript-first agent framework with built-in memory and observability.
summary: TS-native agent framework. Built-in memory (Observational Memory), workflow primitives, and observability. Strong choice when your stack is already Next.js / Vercel.

name: n8n
one_liner: Open-source workflow automation with an AI-friendly node ecosystem.
summary: The OSS Zapier — visual workflow builder with hundreds of integrations. Increasingly the default deliverable for 'automation as a service' shops; a community library of AI templates makes it easy to ship copy-paste agents.

name: Make.com
one_liner: Hosted visual workflow automation — Zapier alternative with deeper logic.
summary: Hosted no-code workflow builder. Less open than n8n but easier to deploy for non-technical operators. Strong AI module integrations.

name: Browserbase
one_liner: Hosted, scalable headless-browser infrastructure for AI agents.
summary: Runs headless browsers as a service so AI agents and scrapers don't have to manage Playwright fleets, proxies, captcha handling, or session persistence. Pairs naturally with Stagehand at the agent layer.

name: Stagehand
one_liner: Open-source AI browsing framework: act, extract, observe.
summary: Wraps Playwright with three primitives — `act`, `extract`, `observe` — so an LLM can drive a browser at the level of natural-language intents rather than CSS selectors. Designed to run on top of Browserbase or a local Playwright.

name: Playwright
one_liner: Microsoft's cross-browser automation library — the substrate Stagehand sits on.
summary: Modern browser automation library from Microsoft. Cross-browser (Chromium, Firefox, WebKit), strong networking primitives, headed/headless modes. The de facto base for agentic browsers.

name: Browser Use
one_liner: Open-source 'make any LLM use a browser' library.
summary: Python framework for giving any LLM a browser. Action-space focused on natural-language → DOM interactions; popular in the open-source agent stack as a Stagehand alternative.

name: Skyvern
one_liner: Browser-agent platform for automating workflows on any website.
summary: Skyvern is a browser-agent product with a hosted UI; under the hood it's open-source. Strong on form-filling and multi-step business flows that don't have APIs.

name: Exa
one_liner: Neural search API plus an excellent MCP server.
summary: Search API designed for LLMs: semantic over the open web, plus specialised endpoints for GitHub, LinkedIn, academic search, and find-similar. Their MCP server is one of the strongest off-the-shelf research tools for agents.

name: Apify
one_liner: Marketplace of pre-built scraping 'actors' — APIs and MCP.
summary: Hosts thousands of pre-built scrapers ('actors') for everything from Show HN to TikTok comments. Call them as APIs (or via the MCP server) and get structured JSON. The 'website-content-crawler' and 'rag-web-browser' actors handle JS-heavy product sites.

name: Firecrawl
one_liner: Crawl + scrape any website into clean markdown for LLMs.
summary: Normalises web pages into LLM-ready markdown with structured metadata. Good when you want a single API to feed RAG pipelines without writing site-specific scrapers. OSS self-host option exists.

name: Clay
one_liner: GTM data platform with a built-in agent ('Claygent').
summary: Spreadsheet-like GTM data platform sales teams use to enrich leads, find waterfall data, and run Claygent — an agent that can scrape, search, and call APIs to fill any cell. Strong for B2B prospecting.

name: Mem0
one_liner: Long-term memory layer for AI agents.
summary: Stores user-level facts and retrieves them at query time via a vector + graph index. Decides ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NONE per turn via an LLM judge prompt. Easy drop-in for chat apps that need 'remember my preferences' behaviour.

name: Supermemory.ai
one_liner: Hosted long-term memory API.
summary: Hosted memory API with first-class concepts like 'spaces' (per-user contexts), graph-backed retrieval, and built-in deduplication. Less battle-tested than Mem0 but more product-shaped.

name: Zep
one_liner: Temporal knowledge-graph memory for AI agents.
summary: Memory built on a temporal knowledge graph (Graphiti). Edges have valid-time intervals; gives clean handling of facts that change over time. Hosted + OSS self-host.

name: ElevenLabs
one_liner: State-of-the-art voice synthesis API.
summary: Default voice-synthesis API for production AI voice apps in 2026 — best quality on most languages, fast streaming, voice cloning. Pairs with HeyGen for lipsync video.

name: HeyGen
one_liner: Video avatar generation with lipsync and natural delivery.
summary: Generates talking-avatar videos from a script. Strong lipsync, lots of avatar templates, supports custom-cloned avatars. Common pairing with ElevenLabs voices for end-to-end video.

name: Vercel
one_liner: Frontend + edge-function hosting; the default for Next.js apps.
summary: Hosts Next.js apps and Edge Functions. Tight integration with the Vercel AI SDK; fastest deployment path for streaming AI UIs. Free tier handles MVP traffic.

name: Supabase
one_liner: Open-source Firebase alternative — Postgres + auth + storage + pgvector.
summary: Hosted Postgres with auth, storage, realtime, edge functions, and (crucially) pgvector pre-installed. The default backend for indie/MVP AI apps that need a relational DB plus vector search.

name: Modal
one_liner: Serverless GPU runtime for Python — deploy a model in 5 lines.
summary: Serverless containers with first-class GPU support. The fastest way to deploy a custom-trained model or run a Python agent that needs scale. Pay-per-second.

name: Replicate
one_liner: Run open-source models via API — image, audio, video, language.
summary: Hosts thousands of open-source models behind a unified API. Great for image/audio/video where the model variety is the value (Flux, SDXL, MusicGen, etc.).

name: Pinecone
one_liner: Hosted vector database — production-grade ANN.
summary: Hosted vector DB, mature operations, fast at any scale. Default 'I need a vector store and don't want to think about it' choice. More expensive than self-hosted alternatives like pgvector or Qdrant.

name: Qdrant
one_liner: Open-source vector DB with hosted option.
summary: Rust-based open-source vector database with strong filtering and hybrid-search support. Self-host if you want control; managed cloud if you don't.

name: Resend
one_liner: Modern transactional email API for developers.
summary: Transactional email API built for developers — react-email templating, deliverability tooling, audience management. Replaces SendGrid in modern stacks.

name: Twilio
one_liner: SMS, voice, WhatsApp, and email APIs.
summary: Long-standing communications platform: SMS, voice, WhatsApp, email. The default channel layer for non-email notifications and the backbone of most voice-agent products.

name: Slack MCP Server
one_liner: MCP server exposing Slack actions to any MCP client.
summary: Reference MCP server for Slack — read channels, send messages, list users. Lets any MCP-compatible agent (Claude Code, Cursor) act on Slack without bespoke integration code.

name: Tinker
one_liner: Managed RL fine-tuning service from Thinking Machines Lab.
summary: Hosted RL training as an API — exposes forward/backward/optim-step over LoRA adapters on open-weight base models. Used by mempol and other GRPO recipes; the right choice when you want RL fine-tuning without owning a GPU cluster.

name: DeepWiki
one_liner: Auto-generated structured wiki for any GitHub repo, by Devin.
summary: Cognition's product that auto-generates a structured wiki for any public GitHub repo. Useful as a sub-tool for an agent that needs structured docs on a specific component without us maintaining them.

name: v0
one_liner: Vercel's AI UI scaffolder — text → React/Tailwind components.
summary: Generates production-ready React + Tailwind UIs from natural language. Output is code you own, not a black box. Default UI prototyping tool when paired with Vercel hosting.

name: Lovable
one_liner: Full-stack AI app builder — frontend + backend + DB.
summary: Goes further than v0: generates the database, API routes, and frontend together. Less code-first; aimed at fast complete-app prototyping.

name: Bolt
one_liner: Browser-based AI app builder by StackBlitz.
summary: Runs the entire dev environment in the browser via WebContainers. Edit + preview live. Strong for prototyping; deploy targets are Netlify / Vercel.
